messages:
lucas: heads up — multiple production customers in Brazil reporting 700-1200ms p95 and intermittent 401s this morning. started ~07:10 BRT. :rotating_light:

tina: seeing the same in our monitoring dashboards, spike in requests routed to us-east-1 vs sa-east-1. latency + auth failures correlate.

kevin: any idea if this is a model variant fallback or pure routing?

lucas: initial traces show requests are reaching our us-east infra, not the SA pop. tokens that are region-scoped sometimes return 401 when validated in wrong region. also 3 customers reported ~20% request retries (client-side) -> billing surge.

maya: customer impact: 3 enterprise tenants, some 429s and increased costs. they're asking for repro steps and mitigation now.

sre-bot: Alert: POP-mismatch detected. % of traffic for sa-east-region served by us-east increased from 1% -> 32% between 07:08-07:22 UTC.

kevin: can someone run a quick dig from a Brazil resolver? suspect ISP resolver cache returning old anycast IPs from prior deployment.

lucas: ran this from my laptop (Vivo ISP):
```
$ dig +short example.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
34.200.10.11
```
That's an us-east address (ASN mapping). expected sa-east anycast pool 150.95.x.x.

kevin: ran dig +trace via a Cloudflare resolver (1.1.1.1):
```
;; Received 127.0.0.1#53
example.redwood.ai. 300 IN A 150.95.21.7
```
So authoritative shows SA IP, but some resolvers still return the old answer.

lucas: looks like ISP/edge caches have a stale record. our GeoIP DB was updated yesterday and we rolled the sa-east announcement; TTL on the old record was set to 3600 accidentally for a subset of delegations.

tina: that matches customer reports: they started seeing problems ~30-45m after our roll — exactly when caches outside our control would still hold the old mapping.

kevin: repro steps for support: 1) ask customer to run `dig example.redwood.ai +short` and `dig +trace` 2) if they see us-east IP, `sudo killall -HUP systemd-resolved` or flush OS DNS; 3) if on Android/ISP mobile, often nothing helps until resolver TTL expires or ISP clears cache. include the packet capture lines we want.

maya: can we provide an interim mitigation? customers want immediate fix (they're hitting 401s).

lucas: temporary mitigation options: 1) issue a short-lived redirect at our CDN edge to forward to sa-east (risk: increases edge complexity), 2) add token validation fallback logic to accept region-scoped tokens validated in another region for 30m window (safer), 3) ask support to advise clients to flush local DNS and rotate tokens.

kevin: option 2 seems fastest codewise. i'll prototype a fallback that checks token signature against global KMS and log region mismatch events — we can gate by a rollout flag. low-risk?

lucas: agreed. also update our DNS provisioning to never set >300 TTL for region-swappable entries and add a pre-roll check to detect long TTLs. open followups: infra ticket and a support KB.

ops-bot: Created ticket INFRA-1887 "Fix long TTL on regional DNS publishes + pre-roll validation" assigned to eng-infra.

maya: i'll draft the support KB with repro commands, recommended client steps, and the escalation message. will include sample `dig` output and curl trace: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://example.redwood.ai/v1/predict`

tina: can we also push a quick info note to customers in affected orgs that we're deploying a fallback change? want to avoid surprise billing.

lucas: yes — coordinate with account reps. I'll land a canary for token fallback in sa-east tonight and monitor.

kevin: putting a small checklist here for post-mitigation: 1) confirm traffic shifts back to sa-east 2) monitor auth 401 rate 3) check for billing retry spikes 4) validate DNS TTLs across major ISP resolvers via probes.

maya: confirmed — customers acknowledged receipt and asked for ETA. passing to account team. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: INFO: Canary rollout started for token-fallback (5% of sa-east traffic) at 3309991290.

lucas: thanks team — keep updates in this thread. if anyone sees additional resolver anomalies, paste the dig output here. :eyes:
